subproblem.title: L¹(ν) approximation of a unit-bounded measurable covector field by smooth unit-bounded test forms supported in an open set
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let ν be a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open with ν(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, and let β : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n be ν-integrable with covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1 for ν-a.e. x. Then for every ε > 0 there is a smooth compactly supported n-form ω on ℝ^P (IsTestForm ω) with tsupport ω ⊆ V, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1 for every x, and ∫⁻ ofReal(covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x − β x)) dν(x) < ofReal ε.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), IsFiniteMeasure ν → IsOpen V → ν Vᶜ = 0 → Integrable β ν → (∀ᵐ x ∂ν, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - β x)) ∂ν < ENNReal.ofReal ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 3–4: inner regularity, L¹-density of continuous compactly supported maps, radial retraction, smoothing and a smooth cut-off. Here the compact core is chosen inside V. Two details are simplified relative to the parent text:
- the retraction estimate uses the factor 2, which is valid for any seminorm, instead of the 1-Lipschitz property;
- the bound N ≤ 1 after smoothing comes from rescaling a uniform smooth approximation, instead of from the convexity of mollification.

Notation. F := Covector (Euclid P) n with its operator norm ‖·‖; F is a complete real normed space. Lean infers CompleteSpace for F; no FiniteDimensional instance is used. N := covectorEuclideanNorm. 𝓘 := the set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P. For the standard basis e_j, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}). m := ν(ℝ^P), a finite real number ≥ 0. "a.e." always refers to ν.

1. Properties of N.
- N(α) = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2} = ‖c(α)‖₂, where c : F → ℝ^𝓘, c(α) := (α(e_I))_{I∈𝓘}, is linear and ‖·‖₂ is the Euclidean norm. Hence N(α) ≥ 0, N(0) = 0, N(tα) = |t|·N(α), and N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α').
- |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ C‖α‖ with C := (#𝓘)^{1/2}.
- Consequently |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is continuous.

2. Compact core. For j ≥ 1 let K_j := {y : ‖y‖ ≤ j and B(y, 1/j) ⊆ V}.
- For r > 0 the set {y : B(y, r) ⊆ V} is closed: if y_k → y with B(y_k, r) ⊆ V and |z − y| < r, then |z − y_k| < r for large k, so z ∈ V.
- Hence K_j is closed and bounded, so compact. Also K_j ⊆ V, K_j ⊆ K_{j+1}, and ⋃_j K_j = V because V is open.
- ν is finite and the measurable sets V ∖ K_j decrease to ∅, so ν(V ∖ K_j) → 0. Moreover ν(ℝ^P ∖ K_j) = ν(ℝ^P ∖ V) + ν(V ∖ K_j) = ν(V ∖ K_j).
- Fix K := K_j with ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < ε/8.
- Alternative: Measure.InnerRegularWRT.isCompact_isClosed composed with Measure.InnerRegularWRT.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace gives a compact K ⊆ V with ν(K) > ν(V) − ε/8 directly.

3. Continuous approximation. ν is a finite Borel measure on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P, hence regular, and ℝ^P is locally compact. Continuous compactly supported maps are dense in L¹(ν; F) (Mathlib: Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le). So there is a continuous g : ℝ^P → F with compact support and ∫ ‖g(x) − β(x)‖ dν(x) ≤ ε/(8(C + 1)).

4. Retraction. Define π : F → F by π(a) := max(1, N(a))⁻¹·a.
- π is continuous (N is continuous and max(1, N) ≥ 1), π(0) = 0, and N(π(a)) = N(a)/max(1, N(a)) ≤ 1.
- Claim: N(π(a) − b) ≤ 2N(a − b) whenever N(b) ≤ 1. If N(a) ≤ 1, then π(a) = a. Otherwise π(a) = a/N(a) and N(a − π(a)) = (1 − 1/N(a))·N(a) = N(a) − 1 ≤ N(a) − N(b) ≤ N(a − b). So N(π(a) − b) ≤ N(π(a) − a) + N(a − b) ≤ 2N(a − b).
- Put g₁ := π ∘ g. Then g₁ is continuous, has compact support (g₁(x) = 0 whenever g(x) = 0), and N(g₁(x)) ≤ 1 for all x.
- For a.e. x (namely where N(β(x)) ≤ 1): N(g₁(x) − β(x)) ≤ 2N(g(x) − β(x)) ≤ 2C‖g(x) − β(x)‖.

5. Smoothing. g₁ is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous. Let η := ε/(8(C + 1)(m + 1)) > 0.
- There is a C^∞ map g₂' : ℝ^P → F with ‖g₂'(x) − g₁(x)‖ < η for every x: convolve g₁ with a smooth mollifier of sufficiently small radius (Mathlib: UniformContinuous.exists_contDiff_dist_le).
- Put g₂ := (1 + Cη)⁻¹·g₂', which is C^∞.
- For every x, N(g₂'(x)) ≤ N(g₁(x)) + N(g₂'(x) − g₁(x)) ≤ 1 + Cη, hence N(g₂(x)) ≤ 1.
- Also N(g₂(x) − g₁(x)) ≤ N(g₂(x) − g₂'(x)) + N(g₂'(x) − g₁(x)) = (Cη/(1 + Cη))·N(g₂'(x)) + N(g₂'(x) − g₁(x)) ≤ Cη + Cη = 2Cη.

6. Cut-off.
- K is compact, V is open, K ⊆ V, and ℝ^P is locally compact Hausdorff. So there is an open V₀ with K ⊆ V₀, closure V₀ compact and closure V₀ ⊆ V.
- By the smooth Urysohn lemma (Mathlib: exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff, applied to the open set V₀ and the closed set K ⊆ V₀), there is a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with support χ = V₀ and χ = 1 on K. Then tsupport χ = closure V₀ is compact and contained in V.
- Define ω(x) := χ(x)·g₂(x). Then ω is C^∞ (a product of C^∞ maps), tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ V, and ω has compact support. So IsTestForm ω and tsupport ω ⊆ V.
- N(ω(x)) = χ(x)·N(g₂(x)) ≤ 1 for every x.

7. Estimate. Let x satisfy N(β(x)) ≤ 1 and the inequality of step 4; this holds for a.e. x.
- If x ∈ K, then ω(x) = g₂(x), so N(ω(x) − β(x)) ≤ N(g₂(x) − g₁(x)) + N(g₁(x) − β(x)) ≤ 2Cη + 2C‖g(x) − β(x)‖.
- If x ∉ K, then N(ω(x) − β(x)) ≤ N(ω(x)) + N(β(x)) ≤ 2.
- Hence, a.e., ENNReal.ofReal(N(ω(x) − β(x))) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(2Cη) + ENNReal.ofReal(2C‖g(x) − β(x)‖) + 2·1_{ℝ^P∖K}(x).
- g − β is integrable, so ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal‖g − β‖ dν = ENNReal.ofReal ∫ ‖g − β‖ dν. Integrating the bound: ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(N(ω − β)) dν ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(2Cηm + 2C·∫ ‖g − β‖ dν) + 2ν(ℝ^P ∖ K).
- Here 2Cηm = 2Cmε/(8(C + 1)(m + 1)) < ε/4 and 2C·∫ ‖g − β‖ dν ≤ 2Cε/(8(C + 1)) < ε/4, so the first term is ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(ε/2). Also 2ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < ENNReal.ofReal(ε/4).
- So ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(N(ω − β)) dν < ENNReal.ofReal(ε/2) + ENNReal.ofReal(ε/4) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε.
Thus ω has all the required properties.

Lean note. Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le lives in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense, and UniformContinuous.exists_contDiff_dist_le lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.SmoothApprox. Neither module is in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, so an implementation must import them or reprove these facts. With the imports, both apply to Covector (Euclid P) n-valued maps, and the regularity instance for ν follows from IsFiniteMeasure ν via Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure. exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff and exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure are already available.
proof_key_steps: N = covectorEuclideanNorm is a continuous seminorm with N ≤ C‖·‖.
Inner regularity: a compact K ⊆ V with ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < ε/8, from the exhaustion K_j = {‖y‖ ≤ j, B(y,1/j) ⊆ V}.
L¹(ν; F) density: a continuous compactly supported g with ∫‖g − β‖ dν small.
Radial retraction π(a) = a/max(1, N(a)): g₁ = π∘g has N ≤ 1 and N(g₁ − β) ≤ 2N(g − β) a.e.
Smooth uniform approximation g₂' of g₁, rescaled to g₂ = g₂'/(1 + Cη), gives N(g₂) ≤ 1 and N(g₂ − g₁) ≤ 2Cη.
Smooth Urysohn cut-off χ = 1 on K with compact tsupport in V; ω = χ·g₂ is an admissible test form.
Splitting over K and its complement gives ∫⁻ ofReal N(ω − β) dν < ε.

audit.reason: The type includes every analytic hypothesis and the exact support, pointwise bound and strict approximation conclusion. Compact exhaustion, L¹ density, the factor-two retraction estimate, uniform smoothing with rescaling, and cutoff give the stated error bound. The cited pinned APIs apply to the complete covector space with the identified imports; no finite-dimensional codomain assumption or future proof-search obligation is hidden.

subproblem.title: Simon 6.2.6(a)–(b) for the Euclidean coefficient norm: a unit simple n-vector has dual norm 1, attained by one fixed linear map J
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let F = Covector (Euclid P) n be the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P (continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ), let n-vectors be the continuous linear functionals ξ : F → ℝ (MultiVector P n, with ⟨α, ξ⟩ = ξ(α)), and let |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, summed over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P}. Then there is one continuous linear map J : MultiVector P n → F such that for every n-vector ξ and every subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q (that is, ξ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τ_n) for all α, for an orthonormal family τ spanning Q): (i) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ F; (ii) |J(ξ)| = 1; (iii) ξ(J(ξ)) = 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ J : MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ covectorEuclideanNorm (J ξ) = 1 ∧ ξ (J ξ) = 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (linear algebra); Simon Ch. 6, Remark 2.6(a)–(b) (chapter-06.txt lines 238–256), for the inner-product (Euclidean coefficient) norm. Step 3 below is the Cauchy–Binet identity Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauchy%E2%80%93Binet_formula); it is proved here directly from step 1.

Notation. F := Covector (Euclid P) n is the space of continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ. An n-vector is w ∈ MultiVector P n = (F →L[ℝ] ℝ). e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun). For x ∈ ℝ^P, x_j := ⟨x, e_j⟩ is its j-th coordinate, so x = Σ_j x_j e_j. 𝓘 is the finite set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P. For f : Fin n → Fin P put e_f := (e_{f(0)}, …, e_{f(n−1)}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n. By definition N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}; the Lean sum ranges over all I : Fin n → Fin P, with summand 0 unless StrictMono I. For v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and f : Fin n → Fin P let D_f(v) := det[(v_i)_{f(k)}]_{i,k∈Fin n}.

1. Expansion: for all α ∈ F and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^n, α(v) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} D_I(v)·α(e_I).
- Write each argument as v_i = Σ_j (v_i)_j e_j. By multilinearity, α(v) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (∏_i (v_i)_{f(i)})·α(e_f).
- If f is not injective, e_f has two equal entries, so α(e_f) = 0 because α is alternating.
- Every injective f is uniquely f = I∘σ with I ∈ 𝓘 (the increasing enumeration of the n-element set f(Fin n)) and σ ∈ Perm(Fin n) (σ = I⁻¹∘f). Every such pair gives an injective f.
- Since α is alternating, α(e_{I∘σ}) = α(e_I∘σ) = sign(σ)·α(e_I).
- Hence α(v) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)·Σ_σ sign(σ)·∏_i (v_i)_{I(σ(i))} = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)·D_I(v). The last equality is the Leibniz formula det[m_{ik}] = Σ_σ sign(σ)·∏_i m_{i,σ(i)} with m_{ik} = (v_i)_{I(k)}.
- For n = 0, 𝓘 consists of the empty map, D is the determinant of the empty matrix, which is 1, and both sides equal α of the empty tuple.

2. Coordinate covectors. For f : Fin n → Fin P define e^f(v) := D_f(v).
- Row i of the matrix [(v_i)_{f(k)}]_{i,k} depends linearly on v_i alone, and det is linear in each row, so e^f is n-linear.
- If v_i = v_{i'} for some i ≠ i', two rows coincide and the determinant vanishes, so e^f is alternating.
- e^f is continuous. Every entry satisfies |(v_i)_{f(k)}| ≤ ‖v_i‖, and the Leibniz formula has n! terms, each of absolute value ≤ ∏_i ‖v_i‖. So |e^f(v)| ≤ n!·∏_i ‖v_i‖, and a multilinear map with such a bound is continuous. Thus e^f ∈ F.
- Lean note: build e^f with AlternatingMap.mkContinuous and this bound, or as the alternatization of the product of the coordinate functionals v ↦ (v_k)_{f(k)}. The pinned Mathlib has no continuity lemma for multilinear maps on finite-dimensional spaces, and FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n) is not inferred.
- For I, K ∈ 𝓘: e^I(e_K) = det[(e_{K(i)})_{I(k)}]_{i,k} = det[δ_{K(i),I(k)}]_{i,k}. If K = I this is the identity matrix, so e^I(e_I) = 1.
- If K ≠ I: a strictly increasing map is determined by its image, so K(Fin n) ≠ I(Fin n). Both sets have n elements, so some K(i) ∉ I(Fin n). Row i is then zero, and e^I(e_K) = 0.

3. Cauchy–Binet for orthonormal families: if τ : Fin n → ℝ^P is orthonormal, then Σ_{I∈𝓘} D_I(τ)² = 1.
- Let γ(v) := det[⟨v_i, τ_k⟩]_{i,k}. Exactly as in step 2, γ ∈ F; the bound is |γ(v)| ≤ n!·∏_i ‖v_i‖, because |⟨v_i, τ_k⟩| ≤ ‖v_i‖·‖τ_k‖ = ‖v_i‖.
- By orthonormality, γ(τ) = det[⟨τ_i, τ_k⟩] = det(Id) = 1.
- For I ∈ 𝓘, γ(e_I) = det[⟨e_{I(i)}, τ_k⟩]_{i,k} = det[(τ_k)_{I(i)}]_{i,k}. This matrix is the transpose of [(τ_i)_{I(k)}]_{i,k}, so γ(e_I) = D_I(τ).
- Step 1 with α = γ and v = τ gives 1 = γ(τ) = Σ_I D_I(τ)·γ(e_I) = Σ_I D_I(τ)².

4. The map J. Define J(w) := Σ_{I∈𝓘} w(e^I)·e^I for w ∈ MultiVector P n.
- Each w ↦ w(e^I) is evaluation at the fixed covector e^I, a continuous linear functional on MultiVector P n, and the sum is finite. So J : MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] F, and J does not depend on any ξ or Q.
- Lean note: J := Σ_{I∈𝓘} (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ e^I).smulRight e^I typechecks with this type. Avoid LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap, which needs a FiniteDimensional instance that is not inferred.
- By step 2, for K ∈ 𝓘: J(w)(e_K) = Σ_I w(e^I)·e^I(e_K) = w(e^K).
- Therefore N(J(w))² = Σ_{K∈𝓘} w(e^K)².
- By linearity of w, w(J(w)) = Σ_I w(e^I)·w(e^I) = Σ_I w(e^I)².

5. Conclusion. Let ξ ∈ MultiVector P n and Q satisfy IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q. Then there are an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P (spanning Q) and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(α) = s·α(τ) for every α ∈ F.
- (i) For α ∈ F, step 1 gives α(τ) = Σ_I D_I(τ)·α(e_I). By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘 and step 3: |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ (Σ_I D_I(τ)²)^{1/2}·(Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} = N(α).
- (ii) For I ∈ 𝓘, ξ(e^I) = s·e^I(τ) = s·D_I(τ). By steps 4 and 3, N(J(ξ))² = Σ_I s²·D_I(τ)² = 1. Since N ≥ 0, N(J(ξ)) = 1.
- (iii) By steps 4 and 3, ξ(J(ξ)) = Σ_I ξ(e^I)² = Σ_I D_I(τ)² = 1.
This proves the statement with the single map J of step 4. If n > P, then 𝓘 = ∅ and step 3 shows that no orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P exists, so the hypothesis is never satisfied; the argument covers this case unchanged.
proof_key_steps: Expansion: α(v) = Σ_{I strictly increasing} D_I(v)·α(e_I), by multilinearity, alternation and the Leibniz formula.
Coordinate covectors: e^I(v) = det[(v_i)_{I(k)}] lies in F and satisfies e^I(e_K) = δ_{IK} on strictly increasing I, K.
Cauchy–Binet for orthonormal τ: Σ_I D_I(τ)² = 1, by expanding γ(v) = det[⟨v_i, τ_k⟩] at v = τ.
Define J(w) = Σ_I w(e^I)·e^I. It is continuous linear with J(w)(e_K) = w(e^K), so N(Jw)² = Σ_I w(e^I)² = w(Jw).
For ξ = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_n: Cauchy–Schwarz gives |ξ(α)| ≤ N(α), and ξ(e^I) = ±D_I(τ) gives N(Jξ) = 1 and ξ(Jξ) = 1.

audit.reason: The one-line type matches the prose, including one continuous linear J independent of ξ and Q. The determinant expansion, coordinate covectors, Gram-determinant identity and Cauchy–Schwarz argument establish every conclusion without circularity. Continuity is justified explicitly; zero degree and n > P are covered.

subproblem.title: Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_T(W) for an integer multiplicity representation, for every set W
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Then for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) ≤ μ_T(W). Here M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 ∀x} with |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, and μ_T = R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2.

Notation. H := μHE[n]; M := R.carrier; θ := R.mult; ξ := R.orient; μ := R.measure = (H⌞M).withDensity θ, with θ viewed in [0, ∞]; N := covectorEuclideanNorm.

1. Apply the sibling theorem rsd_mw_unit_orientation_dual to P and n, and fix the resulting J. Only its conclusion (i) is used: whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₀ Q, |ξ₀(α)| ≤ N(α) for every covector α.

2. By the field R.orients, for H⌞M-a.e. x there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Let G be the set of x with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ N(α) for all α. By step 1, H⌞M-a.e. x lies in G.

3. By definition, T.massOn W = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal (T ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W}. Here ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W means ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, tsupport ω ⊆ W, and N(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x. So it suffices to prove ENNReal.ofReal (T ω) ≤ μ(W) for every such ω.

4. Fix such an ω. S := tsupport ω is closed, hence measurable, and S ⊆ W. Let f(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)). By R.Represents T, T ω = R.action ω = ∫ f d(H⌞M).

5. Let x ∈ G.
- If x ∈ S, then |f(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)·N(ω(x)) ≤ θ(x).
- If x ∉ S, then x lies outside the closure of the support of ω, so ω(x) = 0 and f(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0.
Hence ‖f(x)‖ₑ = ENNReal.ofReal |f(x)| ≤ θ(x)·1_S(x) for H⌞M-a.e. x.

6. For every real-valued f, integrable or not (a non-integrable f has Bochner integral 0): ENNReal.ofReal (∫ f d(H⌞M)) ≤ ‖∫ f d(H⌞M)‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ d(H⌞M).
- By step 5 and monotonicity of the lower integral (a.e. version), ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ d(H⌞M) ≤ ∫⁻ θ·1_S d(H⌞M) = ∫⁻_S θ d(H⌞M) = μ(S). The last equality is the definition of the measure with density θ, evaluated on the measurable set S.
- Finally μ(S) ≤ μ(W), because S ⊆ W.

7. Thus ENNReal.ofReal (T ω) ≤ μ(W) for every admissible ω. Taking the supremum gives T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W. The proof uses neither the openness of U or W nor the local integrability of θ.

subproblem.title: Lower bound μ_T(W) ≤ M_W(T) for open W ⊆ U
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U with R.Represents T. Then for every open W ⊆ U, μ_T(W) ≤ M_W(T), i.e. R.measure W ≤ T.massOn W, where R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ and T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), spt ω ⊆ W, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1 ∀x}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → R.measure W ≤ T.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 3–6.

Notation. H := μHE[n]; M := R.carrier; θ := R.mult; ξ := R.orient; μ := R.measure = (H⌞M).withDensity θ. F := Covector (Euclid P) n with operator norm ‖·‖. N := covectorEuclideanNorm.

1. Orientation facts. By the sibling theorem rsd_mw_unit_orientation_dual, fix a continuous linear J : MultiVector P n → F such that IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₀ Q implies (∀ α, |ξ₀(α)| ≤ N(α)), N(J(ξ₀)) = 1 and ξ₀(J(ξ₀)) = 1.
- Let G be the set of x for which IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q holds for some Q. By R.orients, H⌞M-a.e. x lies in G.
- μ = (H⌞M).withDensity θ is absolutely continuous with respect to H⌞M. So μ-a.e. x lies in G, and the same holds for every measure absolutely continuous with respect to μ.
- For x ∈ G: (a) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ N(α) for all α; (b) N(J(ξ(x))) = 1 and ξ(x)(J(ξ(x))) = 1; (c) ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1, because ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ and |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖.

2. Reduction. It suffices to show c < T.massOn W for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < μ(W). Indeed, if T.massOn W < μ(W), taking c := T.massOn W would give T.massOn W < T.massOn W. Fix such a c. Then c < ∞; put c₀ := c.toReal ≥ 0, so c = ENNReal.ofReal c₀.

3. Choice of K and V. For j ≥ 1 let K_j := {y : ‖y‖ ≤ j and B(y, 1/j) ⊆ W}.
- K_j is closed (if y_k → y with B(y_k, 1/j) ⊆ W, then B(y, 1/j) ⊆ W) and bounded, hence compact. The K_j increase with j, and their union is W because W is open.
- By continuity of μ from below, μ(K_j) → μ(W) > c. Fix K := K_j with μ(K) > c.
- Alternative: (Measure.InnerRegularWRT.isCompact_isClosed μ).trans (Measure.InnerRegularWRT.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace μ) gives such a compact K ⊆ W directly, for any measure μ on ℝ^P.
- ℝ^P is locally compact Hausdorff and K ⊆ W with W open. So there is an open V with K ⊆ V, closure V compact and closure V ⊆ W.
- Then μ(V) ≥ μ(K) > c. Also μ(V) ≤ μ(closure V) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ closure V} θ dH < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult, since closure V is a compact subset of W ⊆ U. (For measurable A, μ(A) = ∫⁻_{M∩A} θ dH by the definitions of withDensity and restriction.)
- So c₀ < μ(V).toReal. Put ε := (μ(V).toReal − c₀)/2 > 0.

4. Data for the approximation theorem. Let ν := μ⌞V, the restriction of μ to V.
- ν(ℝ^P) = μ(V) < ∞, so ν is a finite measure.
- ν(ℝ^P ∖ V) = μ((ℝ^P ∖ V) ∩ V) = 0; the complement of the open set V is measurable.
- Let β(x) := J(ξ(x)). ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M (field R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient) and J is continuous, so β is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M, hence for ν (ν ≪ μ ≪ H⌞M).
- J is continuous and linear, so it is bounded on the unit ball. Continuity at 0 gives δ > 0 with ‖J(w)‖ < 1 whenever ‖w‖ < δ; by homogeneity, ‖J(w)‖ ≤ C_J := 2/δ whenever ‖w‖ ≤ 1.
- For ν-a.e. x (x ∈ G), ‖β(x)‖ ≤ C_J by 1(c), and N(β(x)) = 1 ≤ 1 by 1(b).
- Lean note: do not use ‖J‖. The norm instance on MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n is not synthesized in the pinned Mathlib. Obtain C_J from Metric.continuous_iff applied to J at 0, with J.continuous retyped to the metric topology (a definitional equality Lean accepts).
- A ν-a.e. bounded, a.e.-strongly measurable function on a finite measure space is integrable, so β ∈ L¹(ν; F).

5. Approximation. Apply the sibling theorem rsd_mw_exists_testForm_approx to P, n, ν, V, β and ε. This gives ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n with IsTestForm ω, tsupport ω ⊆ V, N(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x, and ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(N(ω(x) − β(x))) dν(x) < ENNReal.ofReal ε.

6. Admissibility. tsupport ω ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U. So ω̃ := ⟨ω, ⟨IsTestForm ω, tsupport ω ⊆ U⟩⟩ ∈ TestFormOn U n, and ω̃ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W (tsupport ω ⊆ W and N(ω(x)) ≤ 1). Hence ENNReal.ofReal(T ω̃) ≤ T.massOn W (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).

7. Computing T ω̃. Let h(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)).
- By R.Represents T, T ω̃ = R.action ω = ∫ θ(x)·h(x) d(H⌞M)(x).
- μ is H⌞M with the measurable density θ, viewed as an ℝ≥0-valued function. So ∫ h dμ = ∫ θ·h d(H⌞M); this identity for integrals against a measure with density holds for every h, integrable or not.
- If x ∉ V, then x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and h(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0. Therefore ∫ h dμ = ∫_V h dμ = ∫ h dν.
Thus T ω̃ = ∫ h dν.

8. Estimate.
- h is a.e.-strongly measurable for ν: ξ is, ω is continuous, and the evaluation map (L, a) ↦ L(a) is continuous. Also |h(x)| ≤ N(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for ν-a.e. x by 1(a). So h ∈ L¹(ν).
- Put d(x) := N(ω(x) − β(x)) ≥ 0. d is a.e.-strongly measurable (N is continuous), and ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(d) dν < ENNReal.ofReal ε < ∞. So d ∈ L¹(ν) and ∫ d dν = (∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal(d) dν).toReal < ε.
- For ν-a.e. x (x ∈ G), by linearity of ξ(x) and 1(a), 1(b): h(x) = ξ(x)(β(x)) + ξ(x)(ω(x) − β(x)) ≥ 1 − N(ω(x) − β(x)) = 1 − d(x).
- Integrating: T ω̃ = ∫ h dν ≥ ∫ (1 − d) dν = ν(ℝ^P).toReal − ∫ d dν > μ(V).toReal − ε = (μ(V).toReal + c₀)/2 > c₀.

9. Conclusion. Since T ω̃ > c₀ ≥ 0, c = ENNReal.ofReal c₀ < ENNReal.ofReal(T ω̃) ≤ T.massOn W. As c < μ(W) was arbitrary, R.measure W = μ(W) ≤ T.massOn W. The proof does not use the openness of U.
